description.plain:
A true pop icon, Robyn “Rihanna” Fenty is a singer, actress, and businesswoman from Saint Michael, Barbados. She was first discovered by American record producer Evan Rogers in 2003 and later signed a contract to Def Jam Recordings in 2004, after auditioning for its then-president, JAY-Z.

The following year, in 2005, she released her debut album Music of the Sun and its follow-up, A Girl Like Me, in 2006. Both albums did well commercially, but it wasn’t until the release of her third album, Good Girl Gone Bad, in 2007 that poised Rihanna as an international pop star. It became her first album to receive a Grammy nomination (seven to be exact) and features one of her biggest hits, “Umbrella.”

Moving onto 2009, Rihanna released her fourth studio album, Rated R. It featured a darker and more atmospheric tone from her previous albums. She released her fifth studio album, Loud, the next year in 2010. It marked her return to making dance-pop records. That summer, she featured on Eminem’s smash hit, “Love the Way You Lie” and is one of her most popular features of all time.

Rihanna continued her album streak in 2011 when she released her sixth studio album, Talk That Talk. It’s lead-single, “We Found Love,” became her biggest hit to date, topping the Billboard Hot 100 for ten weeks. The next year, in 2012, she released her seventh studio album, Unapologetic.

2013 ended Rihanna three-year album streak, taking a short break from recording music. Instead, she featured on songs like Wale’s “Bad (Remix)” and Eminem’s “The Monster.” The following year, in 2014, Rihanna left Def Jam Recordings to sign fully with JAY-Z’s Roc Nation.

2015 saw Rihanna’s return to making solo music, releasing singles like “FourFiveSeconds,” “Bitch Better Have My Money” and “American Oxygen.” The following year, in 2016, she released her eighth studio album ANTI.

In 2017, Rih featured on a few hit songs like Kendrick Lamar’s “LOYALTY.” and DJ Khaled’s “Wild Thoughts.” That same year, she announced she began working on her ninth studio album, although a proper release date has yet to be announced.

With all her hard work, Rihanna has become one of the most awarded artists in history, winning 214 in total. Of these awards include nine Grammy Awards, twelve Billboard Music Awards, thirteen American Music Awards, and seven MTV Video Music Awards.

Aside from music, Rihanna has ventured into other affairs like acting, starring in big movies like Ocean’s 8, This Is the End, Battleship, and the animated cartoon, Home. Rih also launched the highly successful cosmetics brand, Fenty Beauty, in 2017 and was also appointed as an Ambassador of Barbados in 2018.

description.plain:
On “Work,” Rihanna seeks a deep, meaningful connection, however the male character she sings to (played by Drake) is only interested in sex. This narrative is similar to Rihanna and Drake’s previous collaborations, 2010’s “What’s My Name?” and 2011’s “Take Care.”

The song has a distinct dancehall vibe. Rihanna uses Jamaican Patois throughout, with terms like “work” (sex), “haffi” (have to) and “ah go” (going to) appearing in the hook.

Rihanna described her dialect in the song in Vogue’s April 2016 cover story:

You get what I’m saying, but it’s not all the way perfect. Because that’s how we speak in the Caribbean.

On “Work” co-star Drake, Rihanna added: “Everything he does is so amazing. We would go to in the Caribbean and just dance and drink and smoke and flirt.”

Snippets of “Work” began to circulate in January 2016 after the pair were spotted shooting a music video in an L.A. mall. On January 26th, Power 106 DJ Justin Credible tweeted that the  collaboration between Drake and Rihanna would be coming sooner than anticipated.

One of the song’s producers, Allen Ritter, told Genius that the song originally came together at a pool party at Drake’s house.

Both official “Work” videos were released on February 22, 2016.

description.plain:
“Needed Me” is a mid-tempo mood piece with raw lyrics set over top of dark fluttery synth sounds produced by DJ Mustard. Rihanna provides a solid female empowerment anthem with this one (per her fans on Twitter).



It’s basically 3 minutes and 12 seconds of Rihanna serving tea.



This song was cowritten by singer-songwriter Starrah—who’s worked with Jeremih, Kid Ink, and G-Eazy—and Prince Charlez—who’s written for Usher, Enrique Iglesias, and the Backstreet Boys.

description.plain:
“Stay” is the second single off of Rihanna’s seventh studio album Unapologetic.  It features guest vocals from Mikky Ekko and was written by Ekko and Justin Parker.

With this gorgeous piano ballad, Rihanna puts a vulnerable spin on the Brown situation, repeating another theme of the album – failing to resist true love. She inspires melancholy and raw emotion with this track, and never fails to convey her honesty with her lyrics and her delivery.

Chartwise, “Stay” was incredibly successful, moving over 10 million units all together, making it Rih’s third most successful single after “Love the Way You Lie” with Eminem and “We Found Love” with Calvin Harris.

description.plain:
“Kiss It Better” tells the story of a broken relationship. She is aware that no one does it like him so instead of arguing all night she ‘kisses it better’.

A preview of the song first appeared in December 2014—over a year before the release of Anti—on Rihanna’s Instagram page, featuring guitarist Nuno Bettencourt.

https://www.instagram.com/p/wZn2FQBMxx/

In December 2015, a few weeks before the album’s release, the song’s producer, Glass John, took to Twitter and ranted about the delays behind Rihanna’s album. According to Glass John, “Kiss It Better” was supposed to be the first single for Anti, but Travi$ Scott convinced Rihanna to go with “Bitch Better Have My Money” instead. (Travi$ denied John’s claims on Snapchat.)

https://twitter.com/glassjohn/status/680966123911647232
https://twitter.com/glassjohn/status/680966232753885184
https://twitter.com/GlassJohn/status/680964390120628224?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw

John also released a now-deleted 60-second video preview of the track and threatened, “if you don’t say your [sic] sorry "Kiss It Better” isn’t going to come out… how about that?"

According to James Corden, the host of CBS' The Late Late Show With James Corden, Rihanna was supposed to perform this song at the 2016 Grammys. Rihanna ended up cancelling her performance at the last minute due to health issues.

On 31 March 2016, Rihanna released the music video for “Kiss It Better” via her official Vevo account.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=49lY0HqqUVc

In “Sex With Me”, Rihanna makes it clear that having sex with her is something unique; in fact, it’s luxurious and, according to her, “so amazing.”

Rih has definitely mentioned the act on many songs, namely “Birthday Cake”, “Cockiness (Love It)”, “S&M”, “Push Up On Me”, “Watch N' Learn”, and “You Da One.”

On ANTi, she mentions sex multiple times, but it’s different here. Instead of being generally vague lyrics, these are more raw and personal—and just more sexy.

description.plain:
Also stylized as “BBHMM”, “Bitch Better Have My Money” is Rihanna’s second single off her eighth album Anti. The title comes from a scene in the 1988 film I’m Gonna Git You Sucka.

The image used for the single’s cover art seems to come from a shoot Rihanna had in December 2014 in Paris where she modeled a similar look for Paolo Roversi.



On July 1, the highly anticipated 7 minute explicit video was released. Co-directed by Rihanna and French director Megaforce, the video follows the story of Rihanna and her two accomplices kidnapping and torturing a rich accountant’s wife for ransom. It stars Mads Mikkelsen as the accountant. Eric Roberts also makes an appearance as a police officer.

description.plain:
On “Consideration,” Rihanna considers the scope of her career. She wants to be considered a serious artist, not just an entertainer, which to Rih means writing and producing her own work.

On ANTi, Rihanna has a writing credit on every song aside from “Same Ol' Mistakes,” compared to zero writing credits on her fifth album Loud.

Although the song served as the perfect opener for ANTI it was originally intended to be on SZA’s 2017 album Ctrl. In an interview with i-D Magazine , SZA said she performed the song for Rihanna and Pharrell during a writing camp and was reluctant to give it up. SZA even attributed the loss of “Consideration” as part of the reason her own album was so delayed. In the interview she said:

CTRL probably would have been completed a year earlier had I kept Consideration. That was the centerpiece. I shot a video for it and everything.

description.plain:
“Diamonds” was released as the lead single from Rihanna’s seventh studio album, Unapologetic. It became her twelfth number-one in the US.

The song was written by Sia, who wrote the chart topping hit in just 14 minutes.


We’re sitting there trying to make records, and we finally just said, ‘Let’s just do something we like. Let’s make a hip-hop record with some really cool chords on it… It didn’t sound Rihanna at all. We were more thinking of making a record that sounds like Kanye. Let’s make a record with a dope beat. So we did. Then Sia heard the track and instantly gravitated towards it. We weren’t even thinking of putting a pop song on it, but she wrote this amazing song.“
––Benny Blanco (Producer)

I literally punched him in the arm. I thought Benny was playing a trick on me, [Rihanna] could’ve done it her own way, but I think she really genuinely liked the way it was.“
––Sia

description.plain:
Rihanna sings about a “desperado"—someone "on the run,” either literally or metaphorically. She struggles in their relationship and wonders whether she can run away with him or if she will get left behind.

The beat on “Desperado” is an interpolation of the background vocals on alternative-R&B singer Banks‘ song “Waiting Game”.

The song’s producer, Mike Schultz, said that he wanted the song to sound “edgy.”

I like to do different things and try to push the envelope on sound. If you listen to the record, it’s got an alternative vibe but still has urban undertones but it’s guitar and dirty live bass. I was just trying to do something edgy. I’m into doing dark, edgy stuff that moves you, puts you in a mood.

description.plain:
Rihanna comforts her lover by telling him she will be there for him, in good times and bad. The umbrella is a metaphor for her support.

“Umbrella” stayed on top of the UK Singles Chart for 10 consecutive weeks, longer than any other single that decade. The single remained at the top of the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven consecutive weeks.

The accompanying music video, directed by Chris Applebaum, was released on May 11, 2007.

In 2008, “Umbrella” won a Grammy for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration, and was nominated for Record of the Year and Song of the Year. It won two MTV Music Video awards in 2007, but was nominated for three. This song is number 412 on Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.

Mary J. Blige revealed in an interview that this song was actually written by The-Dream and Tricky Stewart for her:

They did the song for me. And it was during the Grammy time and I was really, really busy, and I heard it, and I was like, ‘Oh my goodness, that’s a smash. I love this song.’ And it was like, ‘It’s yours.’ So in the midst of it being mine, they were probably telling [Rihanna] it was hers. She’s such a beautiful lady, and I love her to death. I was so glad that she caught it and knocked it out of the park, and it’s still one of my favorite songs to date.

When Chris Brown and Rihanna were still dating, he recorded his own version of this song. He changed the chorus to “You can be my Cinderella.”

description.plain:
On “What’s My Name?” Drake and Rihanna trade romantic bars about their lovers. In the music video, they play the love interests for each other.

The collaboration was originally planned to be a remix and the solo version to be on Loud but it made the final cut. Ester Dean originally wrote a demo for the song before it was sent to Rihanna to be re-recorded for her album.

The song became an instant hit, eventually giving Rih her eighth number-one and Drake his first. It’s also certified 6x platinum by the RIAA.

description.plain:
“Same Ol’ Mistakes,” is a cover of Tame Impala’s 2015  Currents closer “New Person, Same Old Mistakes.”

During the making of ANTi Rihanna said she wanted  “songs that I could perform in 15 years; I wanted an album that I could perform in 15 years, not any songs that were burnt out.”



Tame Impala’s team issued a statement to NME about Rihanna’s cover:

The Roc Nation team got in touch with us here at Spinning Top letting us know that Rihanna loved… ‘'New Person, Same Old Mistakes.’ They asked if she could cover the song for her new record. Kevin was more than happy to send it her way. We’re all really happy with how the song turned out, love it!

description.plain:
“Loveeeeeee Song” is the first collaboration between Rihanna and trap-rapper Future. The track was released as the fourth single from her seventh studio album Unapologetic on April 3, 2013, peaking at #55 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart during March of that year.

Co-producer Luney Tunez discussed the track’s creation during an interview with Complex:

that was one of the beats I really don’t like. It wasn’t one of my favorites. When I made it, I was in the mindset of being real, melodic, laid back, and sexy.

Future also gave insight to his contribution to the song during an interview with MTV News:

It was a record that I didn’t spend that much time on either. Less thought, [so] it was more natural.

“Loveeeeeee Song” eventually became certified platinum by the RIAA on October 12, 2016.

description.plain:
A sequel to the original Eminem/Rihanna collaboration “Love the Way You Lie”, this song instead looks at the situation from the female perspective, with Rihanna taking lead this time around.

Following the release and commercial success of the original Eminem felt they should record a sequel to/an alternate version of the song. In an interview with MTV, Rihanna stated that initially she was “very against” recording a sequel, saying:

When I first heard the idea about doing a part two, I was just completely against it. I just felt like you couldn’t beat the original. There’s no way you can outdo that, so why compete with it?

She went on to say that when she heard the original “broken down” demo version of the song in the studio with Eminem, sung by American singer-songwriter Skylar Grey, all of her reservations about recording it went away.

See the original Skylar Grey demo below:
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=awJS4GYyYeA

A sequel to the original Eminem/Rihanna collaboration “Love the Way You Lie”, this song instead looks at the situation from the female perspective, with Rihanna taking lead this time around.

Following the release and commercial success of the original Eminem felt they should record a sequel to/an alternate version of the song. In an interview with MTV, Rihanna stated that initially she was “very against” recording a sequel, saying:

When I first heard the idea about doing a part two, I was just completely against it. I just felt like you couldn’t beat the original. There’s no way you can outdo that, so why compete with it?

She went on to say that when she heard the original “broken down” demo version of the song in the studio with Eminem, sung by American singer-songwriter Skylar Grey, all of her reservations about recording it went away.

See the original Skylar Grey demo below:
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=awJS4GYyYeA

description.plain:
According to songwriter Bibi Bourelly, “Higher” was written in only 20 minutes.  She spoke to Vice about the song:

Everything happens for a reason. Working with Rihanna has changed my life. The 20 minutes it took me to write “Higher” is actually what changed my life, because, even though we wrote “Bitch Better Have My Money” first, she heard that one first.

The intoxicating ANTI track first surfaced in March 2015 as a pair of Instagram previews posted by Rihanna while drunk on whiskey at 5:00 AM.

Rihanna compared the song to “a drunk voicemail” in Vogue’s April 2016 cover story:

You know he’s wrong, and then you get drunk and you’re like, ‘I could forgive him. I could call him. I could make up with him.’ Just, desperate.

description.plain:
Album-closer “Close to You” is a haunting piano ballad reminiscent of Rihanna’s 2012 stand-out track “Stay.” Lyrically, the song deals with the singer’s struggle  to move on from a past love.

Frequent Rihanna-collaborator and co-writer for “Close to You,” James Fauntleroy talked about the making of this R&B ballad:


Whenever I’m writing songs for Rihanna, I’m always thinking about specific things that we all know about her, but I’m also trying to make it something that everyone can relate to. “Close to You” is about some things that I know she feels but that people also feel in general.

When you’re thinking of any famous person that’s had a relationship in the media, you remember that everybody has had that feeling and moment when they’re alone and feeling sad. But people are more likely to pretend that nothing is wrong with them than the opposite.

description.plain:
“Woo” is the  only track with a credited feature from Rihanna’s rumored-boyfriend Travis Scott. Abel Tesfaye (The Weeknd) is credited as one of the track’s composers/lyricists. His demo of the song was leaked online on June 7, 2018.



Like other songs on ANTi, “Woo” is a breakup track. In the first verse, Rihanna expresses  contempt towards her ex and his new flame. She exudes her trademark confidence with lines like, “Bet she could never make you cry/Cause the scars on your heart are still mine.”

As the track progresses, Rihanna’s vulnerability comes to the surface, until she finally admits, “I don’t really mean to love ya / I don’t really mean to care about ya, no more.”

“Man Down” is a reggae influenced song which details the murder of a man who was behaving abusively towards Rihanna, as is depicted in the song’s accompanying music video.

description.plain:
“S&M” is an ode to sex, sadomasochism, bondage, and BDSM fetishes. It was released as the fourth single for Loud.

In a 2010 Spin interview, Rihanna said the sexual lyrics aren’t to be taken “too literally” but to be taken more of a metaphorically way to critics:

I don’t think of it in a sexual way, I’m thinking metaphorically. It’s more of a thing to say that people can talk….people are going to talk about you, you can’t stop that. You just have to be that strong person and know who you are so that stuff just bounces off. And I thought it was super bad ass.

The risqué music video featured Rihanna fully nude, which resulted in a immediate ban in multiple countries and flagged on YouTube for mature content, although it’s been since removed.

“Never Ending” includes writing credits for Dido and Paul Herman: the melody in the final two lines of the verse is reminiscent of Dido’s 2000 hit “Thank You,” which Dido and Herman wrote together.

While “Thank You” is a song of appreciation and gratitude, “Never Ending” deals with the conflicting feelings that come with falling in love again after a torturous break-up.

description.plain:
This is a single off Rihanna’s sixth studio album Talk that Talk. It was also included on 18 Months, the third album from Scottish electronic artist and this song’s producer Calvin Harris, who penned the lyrics as well.

This song became one of the bestselling singles of all time, and Rihanna’s longest running single, outlasting her smash hit “Umbrella” on top of the Billboard Hot 100 charts. This was Harris' first time on the Hot 100, and became a huge boon to his career. He’d been releasing music since 2007. Harris said:

It changed absolutely everything. Career-wise it was the best thing that could ever have happened. For example, in America my tune ‘Feel So Close’ came out about three months before. But when ‘We Found Love’ came out, the radio started playing ‘Feel So Close’ like it was the single after. Then that did really well, it charted well and sold a lot of copies."

Harris was able to tap Rihanna for the song after he opening for her on a leg of her Loud tour in 2011. When Rihanna announced the collaboration to Twitter fans, the Rihanna Navy jumped on Harris, ensuring he would produce a hit. Luckily he didn’t disappoint.

The original version of the song was recorded by UK singer Leona Lewis. She told NME:

It was a bit annoying to see how big a hit it was but if I’d released it maybe it wouldn’t have done as well.

The music video, directed by Melissa Matsoukas,  depicts two lovers are in an unsustainable relationship based on passion and drugs, more like an addiction than a healthy interest. The video features a lot of drug usage and a Chris Brown lookalike, which was controversial, given their real-life abusive relationship. Matsoukas addressed the rumors about the controversial video in an interview with MTV:

body.plain:
This is a single off Rihanna’s sixth studio album Talk that Talk. It was also included on 18 Months, the third album from Scottish electronic artist and this song’s producer Calvin Harris, who penned the lyrics as well.

This song became one of the bestselling singles of all time, and Rihanna’s longest running single, outlasting her smash hit “Umbrella” on top of the Billboard Hot 100 charts. This was Harris' first time on the Hot 100, and became a huge boon to his career. He’d been releasing music since 2007. Harris said:

It changed absolutely everything. Career-wise it was the best thing that could ever have happened. For example, in America my tune ‘Feel So Close’ came out about three months before. But when ‘We Found Love’ came out, the radio started playing ‘Feel So Close’ like it was the single after. Then that did really well, it charted well and sold a lot of copies."

Harris was able to tap Rihanna for the song after he opening for her on a leg of her Loud tour in 2011. When Rihanna announced the collaboration to Twitter fans, the Rihanna Navy jumped on Harris, ensuring he would produce a hit. Luckily he didn’t disappoint.

The original version of the song was recorded by UK singer Leona Lewis. She told NME:

It was a bit annoying to see how big a hit it was but if I’d released it maybe it wouldn’t have done as well.

The music video, directed by Melissa Matsoukas,  depicts two lovers are in an unsustainable relationship based on passion and drugs, more like an addiction than a healthy interest. The video features a lot of drug usage and a Chris Brown lookalike, which was controversial, given their real-life abusive relationship. Matsoukas addressed the rumors about the controversial video in an interview with MTV:

Again, it goes back to a story that we all can relate to. It’s not Rihanna’s story; it’s her story in the video, and she’s acting. But everybody’s [as well]. Obviously, there’s a lot of comparisons to her real life , and that’s not at all the intention.

“James Joint” is named after one of Rihanna’s co-writers, James Fauntleroy. He confirmed on Twitter that the track was named for him:

https://twitter.com/fauntleroy/status/692523252829310976

Fauntleroy and Rihanna previously worked together on a number of tracks from Rated R, including the singles “Te Amo” and “Wait Your Turn.”

She spoke about the song during her V Magazine cover shoot, saying:

Dude, I’m in love with my interludes. This one called ‘James Joint’ is on constant repeat.

This song was released via RiRi’s website on April 21st, 2015 in celebration of 4/20.

description.plain:
This song is reminiscent of S&M, where she seemingly sings of love and romance, yet the song is actually about being dominant in the bedroom.

Only Girl (In The World) is part of Rihanna’s fifth album, Loud.



An alternate take on this song is that she is saying she wants to be like Eve in the Garden of Eden. In the Book of Genesis the story goes that Adam and then Eve were the first two humans created by God, and that God had originally intended for the two to live together in Eden for eternity.

The “only one” Adam could have “ever loved” in that setting was Eve, who was literally “the only girl in the world” at that time. Also, Eve is said to have been made out of one of Adam’s ribs; hence she’s “the only one who knows [his] heart.” The visuals of the music video for the song seem to support this interpretation of it, with color filters and abstract imagery combining to depict a surreal natural paradise of grassy, flowery plains suggestive of the Garden of Eden.

body.plain:
“Don’t Stop the Music” is an energetic dance-pop track about leaving the stress of life and dancing to the music. It was the fourth single off Good Girl Gone Bad and was promoted by two dance remixes, released on August 7, 2007.

The single peaked at number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 and sold over four million copies in the US.

description.plain:
“Rehab” is about a complicated relationship. While Rihanna loves this person, he treats Rih with scorn. She inexplicably loves him but doesn’t know why.

Though Justin Timberlake is featured on the song, he doesn’t contribute much vocally. He is credited as a co-writer though.

The song managed to peak at 18 on the Billboard Hot 100, continuing Rihanna’s impressive chart performance from Good Girl Gone Bad.

description.plain: This double-song seems to be Rihanna seraching for what everyone is seeking: unconditional love. She thought she could find it through a man, but we are all broken people, unable to give and receive perfect love. Only God can fill the void in our lives and grant us love and peace. She has come to this realization, and is “living in the moment”, not the past, not the future, but NOW in God’s presence. If it is God’s will to end her temporary life on Earth, she is ready, for she knows she will be surrounded by unfailing love. Her pleas to Mother Mary and Jesus, is an expression of her desire to be closer to God, for nothing surpasses his comfort and love.

description.plain:
“Disturbia” was written by Rihanna’s then-boyfriend and fellow recording artist, Chris Brown (alongside his team, the Graffiti Artizts), and was originally intended for his re-release of 2007’s Exclusive. His vocals also can be heard in the background of the song.

Although he still earns royalties for the highly successful record, he apparently regrets writing it for her, for reasons he has yet to reveal.

In an interview with USA Today, Chris spoke on giving the song to Rihanna:

It’s fun being creative and even if you have a concept in your head to write about, you can write it and give it and give it to someone else because it might not personally fit you, but it might be an idea you have.

description.plain:
“Sledgehammer” is part of the original motion picture soundtrack for Star Trek Beyond and was featured in the film’s third theatrical trailer, along with its credits sequence.

A tweet from Rihanna in 2014 suggests that “Sledgehammer” was in the works for over two years. It may have originally been meant for ANTI.

https://twitter.com/rihanna/status/467446357318328322

Sia also receives a writing credit on the song, making this her first collaboration with Rihanna since their 2012 hit, “Diamonds.”

The Star Trek-themed music video was released on June 30. It debuted in IMAX theaters, becoming the first music video ever to do so, although Adele’s “Hello” was the first music video filmed using IMAX cameras.

https://twitter.com/BAHjournalist/status/748524258788319232

description.plain:
“Goodnight Gotham” appears on the deluxe version of Rihanna’s album ANTi. In 2015, it served as the music for Christian Dior’s ad “Secret Garden 4,” also starring Rihanna. The song does not feature any vocals from the singer herself, but contains a sample of Florence and the Machine’s “Only If For a Night.”

During an interview, Florence revealed some information on how the addition of her song came about:

I was so thrilled, ‘cause I’m such a huge fan. … She’d sent me the song and I said, like 'Of course,’ but we never actually managed to speak. I mean, we’ve met before, but we’ve never managed to speak in person about it … We were both really happy. We got to hug it out. … It’s one of my favorite songs from Ceremonials, and I love it when stuff like that happens. When people reimagine your music, I love that, when it has all these different forms."

In December 2014, Rihanna met fans at the Trocadero Square in Paris to be filmed for a video for ANTi. Running down the path, she jumped into the arms of fans and was subsequently surrounded. When the “Goodnight Gotham” video released on July 29, 2016, the footage of the epic meet-and-greet was contained within. The following is the filming of the event as it happened.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-EY32nqkbHs

description.plain:
Musically, “Te Amo” draws influence from Latin American music genres and is set in common time with a tempo of 172 beats per minute. The song is written in the key of G-sharp minor with Rihanna’s vocal range spanning from the low note of F♯3 to the high note of C♯5.
Lyrically, “Te Amo” tells of a relationship between two women, with one realizing that she is falling in love with Rihanna, proclaiming ‘Te amo’ throughout the song. As Rihanna realizes that the other woman is falling in love with her, Rihanna sings “I feel love but I don’t feel that way”, meaning that she knows her suitor loves her, but does not want to become romantically involved with her.

Unlike many other more provocative songs, Rihanna shows her softer and more vulnerable side.

description.plain:
“Cockiness (Love It)” sees Rihanna assuming the role of a dominatrix, confidently telling her lover exactly what she wants from him. Similar themes are explored on “S&M,” which Rihanna released less than a month after this track.

The bass-heavy instrumental was created by Bangladesh, a hip-hop producer best known for his work with Lil Wayne. A remix of “Cockiness (Love It)” featuring A$AP Rocky was released in 2013.

description.plain:
On March 5th, 2015, Rihanna previewed this song that would become the theme song for 2015 March Madness coverage.

https://twitter.com/MarchMadnessTV/status/573661396400910336

A month later, she performed the song live during the March Madness Festival before releasing it exclusively via Jay-Z’s streaming service Tidal a day later on April 5th. The release on Tidal was accompanied with a rather political video depicting several iconic scenes from American history, some controversial, including images from the recent protests surrounding the deaths of Michael Brown and Eric Garner.

According to Billboard’s interview with Sam Harris, “Oxygen” co-writer and member of band X Ambassadors, cites it took him nearly a year to write “American Oxygen.” It began as a track that producer Alex Da Kid had, and slowly but surely, Harris developed from just a title, a backing track and the first two lines to a full-blown song. Harris highlights Bruce Springsteen’s Born in the U.S.A. as a major influence.

“This country is great and has the potential to be something really, really incredible, but there are a lot of problems that we don’t acknowledge and it’s important to shed light on both those things.”

Check out the video:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ao8cGLIMtvg

description.plain:
“You Da One” is a cheerful album opener reminiscent of Rihanna’s previous dancehall-inspired tracks “Man Down” and “We Found Love.” Musically, the song features elements of dubstep, reggae, and house.

The lyrics are simple—Rihanna sings about the excitement (and  relative obsession) that comes with being in a new relationship.

https://twitter.com/rihanna/status/135454417892818945

Many of Rihanna’s previous tracks address skepticism about love and relationships (“Complicated” and “Love The Way You Lie”). On “You Da One” Rihanna throws herself into a relationship head first—she admits she’s “falling hard” but that there’s “nothing wrong with that.”

description.plain:
“Cheers” is the third song on Rihanna’s 5th album Loud. Released August 2, 2011.

Filled with a soundboard of lazy, reggae pop cadence, meant for the ‘semi-alcoholics’. It opens the world of Rihanna as she brushes off the haters and indulges in the weekend. Hitting #4 in the UK, #5 in New Zealand, and #6 in Australia, then finally receiving a 2x Platinum in Australia.

This midtempo collaboration,a song about conflicted love, was the third single from Good Girl Gone Bad. It was co-written by Ne-Yo  and production group StarGate and hit number 7 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Rihanna told MTV:

[Ne-Yo] also did one called ‘Hate That I Love You,’ which is a duet between us. That song, when it first starts off, you think it’s a sexy song, but you have to listen to the lyrics. It’s a really deep song.

description.plain:
In “Where Have You Been”, Rihanna desperately wonders where her lover has been before they met. In fact, she repeats the phrase “where have you been” 14 times in the song, so you know she definitely hoped for a lover to show up.

The song’s gritty electro-pop sound is mainly given by Calvin Harris, who produced another hit on this album: “We Found Love.” Cirkut and Dr. Luke also have production credits.

In the US, the song reached #5 on the Billboard Hot 100, giving Rih her second top ten from the album after “We Found Love”, another track produced by Calvin Harris.

description.plain: Watch N Learn, off of Rihanna’s “Talk That Talk” album, basically explains how she want to turn one of her sex sessions with her man, into a sex lesson. While not trying to criticize her man, she says she wants him to “watch” and “learn”, hence the song title, how to please her. She is willing to teach him all the tricks to do so while also doing some tricks of her own.

description.plain:
“SOS” is the danceable lead single from Rihanna’s A Girl Like Me, and contains more than meets the eye.

The song’s narrative is simply about falling deeply in love, but a sample from Soft Cell’s  “Tainted Love” and multiple references to 80s songs make “SOS” not only catchy, but interesting as well.

The song became RiRi’s first number one on the Hot 100, rising past the #2 peak of her prior best single, “Pon de Replay.” Ten years after its ascension to #1, Rih had added thirteen more number ones, the most recent of which was “Work” featuring Drake.

description.plain:
“Half of Me” was included as the 15th track on the deluxe edition of Rihanna’s seventh studio album, Unapologetic.

Co-written by British singer-songwriter Emeli Sandé, she explained during an April 2013 performance of the track at Hammersmith Apollo that it was inspired by the London Riots that occurred in 2011. This is a story of a person rioting, who to the media seems monstrous but is actually doing so for a cause.

description.plain:
By 2007, Rihanna was established as a hit maker of the highest order, but she hadn’t fully committed to the bad girl persona that would follow her for another decade.

This is the title track, and although it’s not as sonically experimental as some of her later work, with a basic acoustic guitar riff and toned down percussion, her lyrics are pointed. As the final track, the chorus points to the direction her career would now take:

You better learn how to treat us right
Cause once a good girl goes bad, we done forever

Before repeating:

We’re gone forever

This ominous statement may be partially inspired by her manager Jay Z’s lines on his 2001 hit “Song Cry.”

description.plain:
“We Ride” is about an ex-lover, who promised Rih a healthy and faithful relationship, only to break those promises by cheating. In a 2006 MTV interview, Rihanna broke down the song, saying:

[The song] is about this guy saying over and over again, ‘When we ride, we ride, we’re gonna be together until the day that we die’, promising all these things then it turns out he broke all of his promises […] I don’t care if you wanna do that and be ugly and unfaithful, then I can just do my thing, chill with my girls and have fun.

While “We Ride” charted in multiple countries, it failed to chart the Billboard Hot 100. The only other time would occur is with 2009’s “Wait Your Turn.”

“Cold Case Love” is a song recorded by Rihanna for her fourth studio album, Rated R. The song was written by Rob Knox, Justin Timberlake, and James Fauntleroy. Rihanna confirmed in 2010 that the song’s lyrics are indeed about Chris Brown, and their past relationship.

It’s a song that everybody wanted to hear, everything that I didn’t say for the past eight months, exactly how I felt about that relationship and how I feel about it now – that song says it all.

“Wait Your Turn” features Rihanna returning to her island roots, rapping over a heavy reggae dub beat. It was the third single off Rated R.

The song received mixed reviews from critics and was one of two singles not to chart the Billboard Hot 100—the other being 2006’s “We Ride.”

The music video was directed by Anthony Mandler who had previously directed the videos for “Take a Bow” and “Rehab.”

description.plain:
“If It’s Lovin' that You Want” is the flirtatious third track on Rihanna’s Music Of The Sun. The song’s narrative follows RiRi trying to convince a guy to be with her; at least, assuming he wants love.

Released as the follow-up single to her #2 hit “Pon De Replay”, “Lovin” wasn’t as successful, reaching the top ten in only three countries. Still, it reached the top forty within the US, establishing her as not just a one-hit wonder, but a strong pop star that was ready to stay in the market.

description.plain: “Fading” is the fourth track from Rihanna’s fifth studio album, Loud. The song is of the pop/R&B genre and musically samples Irish new-age singer/songwriter Enya’s “One by One”. Lyrically, the song talks of a protagonist who realizes their relationship is fading and decides to move on. The track was noted in nearly all critical reviews of the album as a standout track, praised for its production and Rihanna’s vocal performance.

description.plain:
This is Rihanna’s 4th single off her 2010 studio album Loud.

S&M is an uptempo dance-pop and Eurodance song that samples the synthesizer line from Depeche Mode’s 1984 song “Master and Servant.” In this song, Rihanna metaphorically explains how used to the media’s hard criticism she has become; now using their harsh words and speculations and turning them to work for her.

Although this song was a major hit, many people looked down on its sexual nature and overtly sexual lyrics.

body.plain:
This is Rihanna’s 4th single off her 2010 studio album Loud.

S&M is an uptempo dance-pop and Eurodance song that samples the synthesizer line from Depeche Mode’s 1984 song “Master and Servant.” In this song, Rihanna metaphorically explains how used to the media’s hard criticism she has become; now using their harsh words and speculations and turning them to work for her.

Although this song was a major hit, many people looked down on its sexual nature and overtly sexual lyrics.

description.plain:
“Emergency Room” is a song written by singer-songwriter Priscilla Renea and artist/producer Akon.

It was apparently submitted as a possible duet between Rihanna and R&B singer Mario, however it’s unknown if the song was ever recorded by either artist. A demo of the track featuring vocals by Priscilla and Akon leaked online in 2008.

description.plain: “Break It Off” is a song by Rihanna from her second studio album, A Girl Like Me, and features guest vocals from Sean Paul. The song was written by Donovan Bennett, Sean Paul, K. Ford and Rihanna. The song was released on November 13, 2006, as the album’s fourth and final single. The song was a top 10 hit for Rihanna, peaking #9 on the Billboard Hot 100. No music video was released for the song.

description.plain:
“Same Old Love” was recorded by Rihanna in 2014 for her eight studio album, Anti. The song was later scrapped from the album, and it was eventually recorded and released by Selena Gomez as the second single from her 2015 album Revival

A snippet of Rihanna’s version of the track was leaked on May 4, 2018, with the full version leaking on May 26th, 2020.

The song was written in 2014 during a writing camp organized by producers StarGate and benny blanco. The song started out sounding very different, with writers Ross Golan and Charli XCX freestyling over an uptempo guitar-driven track. Tor, the other half of StarGate, then completely scrapped the backing track and re-worked the song into the piano-driven track known to the public.

description.plain:
Lenny B Club Mix from the International ECD and Digital Promo Maxi



“We Ride” is about an ex-lover, who promised Rih a healthy and faithful relationship, only to break those promises by cheating. In a 2006 MTV interview, Rihanna broke down the song, saying:

[The song] is about this guy saying over and over again, ‘When we ride, we ride, we’re gonna be together until the day that we die’, promising all these things then it turns out he broke all of his promises […] I don’t care if you wanna do that and be ugly and unfaithful, then I can just do my thing, chill with my girls and have fun.

While “We Ride” charted in multiple countries, it failed to chart the Billboard Hot 100. The only other time would occur is with 2009’s “Wait Your Turn.”

description.plain: “Goodbye” is one of Rihanna’s unreleased songs. This captivating piano ballad was originally intended to be on her album Rated R, but it didn’t make the cut. Because so many of the songs and lyrics from Rated R were said to have been about her abusive relationship with Chris Brown, it’s not a long shot that this song might be about him as well, especially given the lyrics about her being tempted to stay in the relationship, but knowing she has to say goodbye instead.

description.plain:
“Hypnotized” follows the theme of Music of the Sun’s tenth track “Rush” where Rihanna talks about the unique feelings she gets when she’s with a special guy. No one else can make her feel the way this guy does; he only has her attention.

description.plain:
On “Should I?” we see Rihanna at a contemplation. This guy keeps taking his shot at her and she isn’t interested in being in a relationship with him. With all his sweet talks, however, it’s getting harder to Rih to say no to him and wonders if she should say otherwise.

J-Status plays the guy in question, where he spits a quick eight bars about how he’s in love with her and needs to be with her.

The song was released as a bonus track on the UK edition and Japanese edition of Music of the Sun.

description.plain:
The fourth single from Rihanna was released on February 19, 2010. The song is about Rihanna taking control in the relationship, including during sex. The song reached the top spot on the Billboard Hot 100 for five consecutive weeks. It became Rihanna’s sixth #1 single.

The music video was directed by Melinda Matsoukas and released on February 9, 2010.

description.plain:
“Joyride” is an unreleased track by singer Rihanna.

The track was originally demoed by Travis Scott and sent to singer-songwriter Tinashe to rework. Soon after, in sessions for her eighth album ANTI Rihanna also decided to record and re-write sections of the track.

Ultimately, Rihanna did not use her version of the track on the final album, choosing instead the Travis Scott collaborations “Woo” and “Pose”.

Tinashe was then free to use her version of the song for her second studio album Joyride, also allowing her to name the album after the track.

description.plain:
“Barz” is an unreleased song by Rihanna that leaked sometime in 2014.

Before a 17-second snippet was found online, many fans believed various tweets from Rihanna contained lyrics to the song, and some dug even further and suggested that Trinidadian-American rapper Nicki Minaj would be a feature on the song. Although some of the tweets' lyrics ended up on songs like “James Joint” from Rihanna’s eighth studio album, not all of them have seen the light of day and are, as of yet, not on any official Rihanna recording.

description.plain: Drive Alone is an unreleased song by the Barbadian recording artist Rihanna. It was formally released by Priscilla Renea in 2018. It is written by Priscilla Renea and Jermaine Jackson amongst others – it is speculated that it was a leftover from LOUD due to it sounding like California King Bed – which was also written by the same producers. Rihanna did record vocals for it.

description.plain: The Other Side is an unreleased song by the Barbadian recording artist Rihanna. All that is known is that this is an outtake from Unapologetic. There’s a picture that shows Rihanna’s old track listing of her seventh studio album. A theory suggests that this song was given to Jason Derulo.

description.plain: Someday is an unreleased song by the Barbadian recording artist Rihanna. All that is known is that this is an outtake from Unapologetic. There’s a picture that shows Rihanna’s old track listing of her seventh studio album. Some fans say that Someday was the best song off of Unapologetic, possibly meaning that this song was quickly leaked and removed before a large audience could hear the song.
